claims.explanation: GW-583340 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 kinase inhibitor, so selective killing is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. The most sensitive lines include EGFR-mutant or ERBB2/ERBB3-altered tumors (HCC4006, BT474, MFE319), while resistant lines are enriched for KRAS/BRAF/PTEN alterations that bypass receptor tyrosine kinase blockade. Additional sensitivity may come from PI3K pathway mutations in receptor-driven lineages, but the dominant predictor is EGFR/ERBB2 pathway activation.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant HCC4006 is among the most killed lines and EGFR is the primary drug target
ERBB2 is a direct drug target and ERBB2-amplified/overexpressing breast cancer lines such as BT474 are sensitive
ERBB3 mutation in MFE319 may support ERBB2/ERBB3 signaling dependence
KRAS mutations are enriched in resistant lines and can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 blockade
BRAF mutations are common in resistant melanoma, thyroid, and colorectal lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K signaling downstream of ERBB and is enriched in resistant lines
PIK3CA mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may cooperate with ERBB dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is seen in resistant melanoma and glioma lines
STK11 mutations appear in resistant lung and other lines, potentially reducing dependence on EGFR signaling
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may reflect broader genomic instability rather than target dependence
TP53 mutations are widespread across both sensitive and resistant lines, so this is weak evidence
